title: Methods and variables in a class

blocks.value: A **method is a collection of statements grouped together to perform an operation.**
Recalling the vocabulary from Lesson 10, now in a class context:

items: The **`void`** keyword denotes that a method is not used to return a value.
A **parameter** is a variable in a method declaration; an **argument** is the actual value passed when the method is invoked.
**The data type of the return value must match the declared return type.** You cannot return an integer from a method declared to return a boolean.
**Instance variables** are declared **outside** any method, constructor, or block. They belong to the object and last as long as it does.
**Local variables** are declared **within** a method definition. They are visible only inside the method that declares them and are not accessible from the rest of the class.

blocks.value: Every `Rectangle` object has its own `length` and `width`. `result` is created fresh each time `area()` runs and disappears when it returns.
**The `this` keyword represents the object receiving the method call, within a method definition.**
It matters most when a parameter has the same name as an instance variable:

Without `this`, the line `name = name;` assigns the parameter to itself and the instance variable never changes, a bug that compiles cleanly and silently does nothing. `this.name` removes the ambiguity.

If you pass an object to `println`, Java prints its class name and a hash code, something like `Rectangle@1b6d3586`, which tells you nothing about its state.
